learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the unstoppable flows of ideas, capital, commodities, and people across borders, and how it transforms our politics, economies, and cultures!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is the fundamental interconnectedness of the world created by the continuous flow of ideas, capital (money), commodities (goods), and people across international boundaries.

Does globalization make states weaker? Yes, by reducing government welfare functions in favor of free markets. However, states also become stronger by using modern technology to better govern and monitor citizens.
Involves greater economic growth and free trade managed by institutions like the IMF and WTO. While it creates immense wealth and choices, it also deepens inequality between the rich and the poor.

Globalisation can lead to Cultural Homogenisation (everyone wearing jeans and eating burgers, leading to a loss of unique cultures) but also Cultural Heterogenisation (cultures mixing to create new, unique combinations, like paneer tikka pizza).

Critics from the political Left argue it makes the rich richer and poor poorer. Critics from the Right worry about the loss of traditional culture and national sovereignty. Forums like WSF (World Social Forum) actively protest it.

fun_activity.title: 👖 The Globalisation Closet
fun_activity.instructions: Open your closet or look at your belongings. Check the tags on your clothes, shoes, and electronics. Make a list of all the different countries where your everyday items were manufactured. You are experiencing the 'flow of commodities'!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define globalization as a multidimensional concept (Political, Economic, Cultural) — it is not just about the economy.
📌 Contrast 'Cultural Homogenisation' (cultures becoming identical, usually Westernized) with 'Cultural Heterogenisation' (cultures mixing and diversifying).
📌 Be prepared to discuss India's experience with globalization, especially the 1991 economic reforms.
quick_recap: ⭐ Technology (telegraph, internet, aviation) is the driving force and primary catalyst for globalization.
⭐ The World Social Forum (WSF) is a major global platform for civil society groups opposing neo-liberal globalization.
⭐ Globalization creates both 'winners' (multinational corporations, skilled workers) and 'losers' (small farmers, traditional artisans).
